review_notes: Source-first scope: the abstract says the paper tests whether earnings-announcement information content changed over time using two Beaver metrics, abnormal trading volume and abnormal return volatility. Section 3 explicitly calls Tables 1 and 2 the primary tests. Retain the full all-quarter pooled specification for both outcomes as parallel main proxies. The separate quarter columns are subgroup/partition analyses, and the rank regressions are robustness checks; Section 4 composition and sensitivity tests are outside the selected baseline family.

The AVAR construction requires firm-quarter market-model estimates and residual variance; retained as a supporting repeated-fit model linked to AVAR. Its fitted parameter estimator is not stated, so it remains unknown. The main regressions use Prais-Winsten GLS; White-corrected standard errors are reported as an inference robustness check.
results_review_notes: The two selected baseline models are the pooled all-quarter primary Prais–Winsten regressions in Tables 1 and 2. Quarter-specific columns and rank-regression statistics are not additional baseline fits.

The Tables 1 and 2 notes identify parenthetical values as t-statistics from primary and rank regressions, respectively. The first t value is retained for each selected primary coefficient; the second rank-regression t value is excluded.
The source reports overall means for AVOL and AVAR in prose (0.94 and 5.33) but gives no variable-level descriptive statistics for TIME, CALDUM, or CALTIME.

The prose reports an unnumbered joint F-test finding for the total time trend b1+b3 among 12/31 firms. It is preserved as an auxiliary joint summary on each selected fit; exact F statistics and other inferential details are unavailable.
